question: In the Hurston exercise, every guess called out in the room was a noun. Why?

options.text: The word follows "on," and the structure of the sentence demands a noun there
options.feedback: You applied syntax without thinking about it: after a preposition like 'on' comes a noun. A model has to learn that same structure, and it does so simply because guessing a verb there would be wrong every time.

options.text: Nouns are the most common words in English, so they are the safest guess
options.feedback: Frequency alone would not stop someone guessing 'the' or 'is,' which are far more common than 'board.' It was the sentence's grammar, not word frequency, that ruled those out.

options.text: Hurston's writing style leans heavily on nouns
options.feedback: Style did come into the game, but at the last step, in choosing 'board' over 'deck.' Knowing the slot needed a noun at all came from grammar, before style entered.

options.text: The slide showed a list of nouns to choose from
options.feedback: No list was shown; the blank was open. Everyone converged on nouns from their own knowledge of how sentences work.
